minutes.headline: Sewer Commission heard a flow-meter vendor on infiltration data and approved prior minutes; legal fee motion got no second.
minutes.summary: The commission heard from Flow Assessment on how the three sewer flow meters are calibrated and checked, and on infiltration and inflow in the system. It also took up the school grease trap level, an engineering procurement for infiltration work, legal fee billing through the town, and agenda items for future meetings. Minutes of 7/30 and 8/14 were approved.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission heard Flow Assessment explain how its three sewer flow meters are calibrated and checked, and what they show on infiltration and inflow.
A motion to have Barb work out a legal fee transfer with the town, based on hours used at the proposed hourly rate, drew no audible second.
Members objected to monthly legal billing that varies with other boards' use of town counsel, and preferred an hourly rate.
Minutes of 7/30 and 8/14 were approved, and first-quarter FY19 sewer bills and a privilege fee commitment were signed.
The open space plan sewer section update was set for the September 11th agenda, and meeting night and frequency for a later agenda.

why_it_matters: How the sewer system's legal costs are billed, by hours used or by a monthly share that moves with other boards' use, decides what sewer ratepayers cover.
The meter and infiltration data bear on whether the system pays to treat groundwater, and on any engineering work later put to ratepayers.
